request: Rank the 4 best Ford Mustang generations overall across the full production run. Use 4 different generations when available, with one representative version from each generation. If the model has fewer than 4 true generations, use the most important era-defining versions across its history.
title: RANKING THE BEST FORD MUSTANG GENERATIONS
close_narration: Which Mustang is your ultimate drive—would you opt for the modern Seventh Gen or the iconic First Gen?
order_rationale: Ranked by weighted enthusiast desirability, driving engagement, historical significance, performance, collectibility, and value—not chronology.

entries.name: Third Generation Mustang GT
entries.label: The Fox-Body Revival
entries.one_line_fact: Let's rank the best Ford Mustang generations. At number four, the Third Generation Mustang GT. Released in 1979 for $6,500, it became a tuner favorite with a 225-hp V8. Its aerodynamic front fascia and rectangular headlights define the Fox-Body era, now valued at $21,000.
entries.ranking_case: The Fox-body Mustang GT revitalized the brand with its lightweight design and tunable 5.0-liter V8.

entries.name: Seventh Generation Mustang GT
entries.label: The Modern Evolution
entries.one_line_fact: Then, the Seventh Generation Mustang GT. In 2024, Ford redefined modern muscle at $35,000, offering a 450-hp V8. With sleeker headlights and a refined front fascia, it keeps the Mustang thrilling for today’s enthusiast.

entries.name: Sixth Generation Mustang GT
entries.label: Global Performance Icon
entries.one_line_fact: The Sixth Generation Mustang GT brings global respect. Starting in 2015 for $32,000, it offered a 435-hp V8 and independent rear suspension. Though some lament the modern features, its fastback profile and quad exhaust tips exude bold charm.
entries.ranking_case: The sixth-generation Mustang GT elevated the model to global performance standards with advanced engineering and design.

entries.label: The Original Pony Car
entries.one_line_fact: Finally, the First Generation Mustang GT takes the crown. In 1965, it sparked a revolution at just $2,366. With a 271-hp V8 and iconic design elements like the long hood and tri-bar taillights, it captured the imagination of the world and remains timeless.
